title: Al-Qur'an: The Lifelong Companion
summary: At this age, the child begins to read fluently. The goal: for the Qur'an to be his daily companion—memorising short surahs, understanding simplified meanings, and connecting verses to his daily behavior.
try_this: Choose a short surah (Ad-Duha, Ash-Sharh, Al-'Adiyat)—memorise one verse together daily, and discuss: What does it mean to you?
reflection_prompts: Which verse does your child love the most? And why?
Have you noticed a change in his behavior after memorisation?

review_defects.arabic: أي آية أحبها طفلك أكثر؟ ولماذا؟
review_defects.english: Which verse does your child love the most? And why?
review_defects.why: The Arabic uses the past tense 'أحبها' (loved), referring to the child's preference during the memorisation process. The English uses the present tense 'does love', shifting the meaning to a general, timeless preference.
